problem: Differential privacy fundamentally trades off privacy for utility in synthetic data generation, and existing approaches don't effectively integrate public data into the privacy mechanism itself.
approach: The paper characterizes the asymptotically optimal domain-aware DP mechanism for histogram-based distribution estimation and introduces PubMix, which explicitly incorporates public data into the privacy mechanism rather than only in pre/post-processing.
contribution: PubMix significantly improves synthetic data quality compared to domain-agnostic privacy mechanisms.

problem: Multimodal fusion systems lack reliable ways to detect low-quality data, sensor noise, and conflicts because existing methods depend on the model's own potentially overconfident predictions.
approach: Geometry-based Multimodal Fusion (GMF) measures data reliability by computing Transport Energy—the physical effort to map noisy data back to the valid manifold—using Diffusion Schrödinger Bridges, acting as an independent judge of data quality.
contribution: GMF significantly improves robustness against severe sensor noise and semantic conflicts by flagging unreliable inputs independently of classifier confidence.

problem: Learning-based PDE control policies trained for fixed sensor/actuator configurations fail when the configuration changes, and multi-agent policies do not scale across different population sizes without retraining.
approach: CINOC reformulates PDE control as operator learning that trains end-to-end through differentiable PDE solvers, producing policies that naturally adapt to varying configurations and exhibit emergent cardinality invariance through agents sharing a common policy.
contribution: CINOC policies trained on small swarms transfer zero-shot to larger populations and tolerate partial agent failure, with convergence to continuous limits proven via mean-field theory.

problem: Unsupervised domain adaptation fixes a single f-divergence measure a priori, which is suboptimal across heterogeneous domain shifts.
approach: The framework tightens the variational bound of f-divergence by learning a monotone Lipschitz transform and selects the divergence family adaptively from data via likelihood-based criterion.
contribution: Achieves more informative discrepancy estimates and consistently improves accuracy on Office-31, Office-Home, Digits, and VisDA-2017.

problem: Dense geometric prediction models lack reliable mechanisms to verify physical causality and can be fooled by edge-like cues that violate surface continuity and occlusion ordering.
approach: Scrambled Edges injects physically invalid edge cues while preserving energy and structure to isolate the effect, measuring whether depth predictors correctly reject unsupported geometric evidence.
contribution: Current depth models show up to 3.2× larger deviation from valid predictions when exposed to Scrambled Edges, and output-level repair recovers only 47% of errors.

problem: Principal component analysis requires full d-dimensional samples, but many applications have hardware limited to only a few scalar measurements per sample.
approach: A compressed variant of Oja's algorithm uses only two adaptive measurements per sample—one along the current estimate and one in random orthogonal direction—with proven optimal convergence.
contribution: Proves tight O(λ₁λ₂d²/(Δ²t)) convergence with matching information-theoretic lower bound, separating fully-observed, adaptive-compressed, and non-adaptive PCA by powers of d.

problem: Developing multimodal research agents faces three challenges: scarcity of search-intensive QA data, lack of effective search trajectories, and prohibitive cost of training with online search APIs.
approach: MM-DeepResearch combines Hyper-Search (hypergraph-based QA generation across modalities), DR-TTS (decomposing tasks into tool experts via tree search), and an offline search engine for RL without costly APIs.
contribution: Develops a powerful multimodal deep research agent showing superiority across benchmarks through offline training and cross-modal information synthesis.

problem: Federated Quantile Regression faces challenges in achieving communication efficiency and optimal statistical guarantees with heterogeneously structured data where agents have distinct feature sets.
approach: Proposes a one-shot weighted ensemble estimator that incorporates scalable weighting schemes to leverage partially observed features at each agent.
contribution: Achieves asymptotic normality with uniformly minimum variance and enjoys strong out-of-sample generalization compared to baselines across various quantile levels.

problem: Robots struggle to manipulate deformable linear objects (ropes, cables) due to narrow task-specific approaches, reliance on real-world data, and lack of simulation environments modeling diverse material behaviors.
approach: DLO-Lab introduces a differentiable simulator for versatile DLO manipulation, a benchmark suite, and a specialized DLO agent that manages topological complexity and grasp sensitivity.
contribution: Enables learning generalizable manipulation skills and demonstrates sim-to-real transfer across tasks with different materials and configurations.

problem: Activations are the primary memory bottleneck in large-batch LLM training, and existing compression methods fail to exploit the spectral structure of activations.
approach: PRAC decomposes activations into a principal subspace (via SVD) and random subspace samples, with precise scaling to achieve unbiased gradient estimation with minimum variance.
contribution: Achieves up to 36% total memory reduction with negligible performance degradation and minimal computational cost on pre-training and fine-tuning tasks.

problem: Full generalist LMs are computationally expensive when deployed as many role-playing characters simultaneously, yet naive pruning destroys role-playing capability by not distinguishing character traits from general knowledge.
approach: Persona-Pruner sculpts lightweight models by isolating persona-specific sub-networks from a character description, using techniques that preserve essential traits while removing redundancy.
contribution: Preserves role-playing performance substantially better than existing pruning methods, reducing performance drop by up to 93.8% while maintaining general LLM capabilities.

problem: KL-regularized multi-armed bandit optimization lacks tight statistical efficiency characterization despite recent improvements in convergence rates.
approach: Sharp analysis of KL-UCB using a novel peeling argument yields tight O(ηK log²T) KL-regularized regret upper bound with linear K dependence, matched by lower bounds.
contribution: First high-probability regret bound with linear K dependence and complete characterization across all regularization intensity regimes.

problem: Sampling from Gibbs distributions in infinite-dimensional function spaces lacks scalable theory and algorithms despite potential for conditional diffusion path sampling.
approach: Functional Adjoint Sampler extends adjoint sampling to Hilbert spaces via stochastic optimal control and stochastic maximum principle, yielding a matching-type objective for functional representation.
contribution: Achieves superior transition path sampling on synthetic potentials and real molecular systems including Alanine Dipeptide and Chignolin.

problem: STM-based molecular assembly requires extensive manual effort and lacks scalable planning frameworks for autonomous nanoscale fabrication.
approach: Combines satisfiability solving for collision-free assembly planning and execution scheduling, with RL agents executing STM manipulation actions in NanoAssemblyGym simulation.
contribution: Demonstrates autonomous assembly of structures containing up to 420 molecules through minimized travel distance and managed corridor allocation.

problem: Machine unlearning techniques have two critical blind spots: over-unlearning that harms retained data near the forget set, and post-hoc relearning attacks that resurrect forgotten knowledge.
approach: Spotter combines masked knowledge-distillation on nearby regions to suppress over-unlearning and intra-class dispersion loss to scatter embeddings and neutralize relearning attacks.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on CIFAR, TinyImageNet, and CASIA-WebFace while providing practical defense against both over-unlearning and prototype relearning.

problem: Unsupervised Camouflaged Object Detection suffers from noisy pseudo-labels and insufficient fine-grained segmentation capability from simple post-processing of DINO features.
approach: DualUCOD uses Dual-Eigenvector Spectral Pseudo-Labeling to fuse semantic and color cues, Boundary-Guided Foreground-Background Refinement for accuracy, and Dual-Branch Contrastive Learning.
contribution: Outperforms existing UCOD methods by generating high-quality pseudo-labels and explicitly incorporating boundary information.

problem: Quaternion self-attention computes component-wise scores with independent softmax operations, increasing computational cost and allowing attention distributions to diverge across components.
approach: Proposes shared-score quaternion self-attention using a single real-valued score from quaternion inner product with shared attention distribution, reducing multiplications by 75%.
contribution: Reduces inference time by up to 44.3% on GPU and 58.1% on CPU in speech enhancement while maintaining quality, with consistent improvements in vision and NLP.

problem: Existing conditional independence testing methods use ML models as surrogates but require train-test splits reducing statistical power, or lack validity guarantees.
approach: Semi-knockoffs accommodates any pre-trained model without splitting data and provides valid p-values and FDR control by requiring only conditional expectations and introducing stability/double-robustness properties.
contribution: Enables valid conditional independence testing with higher statistical power while being less restrictive than model-X assumption methods.

problem: Safety alignment in reasoning models creates a trade-off between safety and utility by explicitly teaching safety rules that rigidly associate rule memorization with refusal.
approach: Adaptive Safe Context Learning (ASCL) frames safety alignment as multi-turn tool-use where models autonomously decide when to consult safety rules, paired with Inverse Frequency Policy Optimization to rebalance advantage.
contribution: Achieves higher overall performance compared to baselines by decoupling rule retrieval from reasoning.

problem: In-context learning for instructional video editing suffers from inaccurate editing regions and token interference between editing and non-editing areas.
approach: ReCo uses width-wise source-target concatenation with latent and attention regularization to increase editing-region discrepancy while reducing non-editing-area changes and suppressing cross-region token interference.
contribution: Superior performance across four instruction-based video editing tasks with a large-scale ReCo-Data dataset of 500K instruction-video pairs.

problem: Privacy in federated and streaming systems must hold for full trajectories under adaptive interaction, but single-edit neighboring user streams defeat standard analysis.
approach: Provides modular recipe: randomized buffering emits bins reducing single-edit streams to Hamming-style updates, enabling any prefix-causal DP mechanism to achieve trajectory-level privacy.
contribution: Achieves trajectory-level (ε,δ)-DP for single-edit streams with explicit privacy-latency link via bin size U.

problem: Conformal prediction for LLM factuality with coherent reasoning graphs is not differentiable, requiring hand-crafted scorers that sacrifice claim retention.
approach: Differentiable Coherent Factuality (DCF) provides a fully differentiable relaxation enabling learned scorers while provably recovering the original algorithm's reliability guarantees.
contribution: Achieves up to 141% improvement in claim retention while maintaining reliability guarantees on reasoning datasets.

problem: Nonlinear conservation laws with uncertainty require treating ill-posed inverse problems, but classical and deep learning methods struggle with proper uncertainty handling.
approach: Frames conservation law simulation as Bayesian inference under Gaussian process priors using recent sparse approximation techniques for scalability.
contribution: Recovers posteriors over nonparametric source fields in seconds while outperforming neural baselines on inverse problems.

problem: Split LLM deployment introduces dual-sided privacy risks: leakage through input prompts and sensitive information through generated response outputs.
approach: PIDI is a two-stage inversion attack targeting both prompts and responses using dual-sided initialization and patched strategy; ADMI defends with adapter-based warmup and mutual information regularization.
contribution: ADMI effectively defends against PIDI and state-of-the-art inversion attacks with minimal task performance impact.

problem: Autonomous driving planners lack explicit self-correction ability—once an unsafe action is proposed, there is no mechanism to correct it.
approach: CorrectionPlanner contains a propose-evaluate-correct loop where a collision critic predicts safety at each step and triggers re-sampling if unsafe, trained with IL and model-based RL.
contribution: Reduces collision rate by over 20% on Waymax and achieves state-of-the-art planning scores on nuPlan.

problem: Training with low-precision quantized weights causes optimization to get stuck at large weight magnitudes due to coarse mantissa resolution.
approach: M+Adam combines additive and multiplicative updates: additive handles sign changes and small magnitudes while multiplicative ensures progress at large magnitudes.
contribution: Consistently improves low-precision training across LLaMA-style pretraining with 60M–1B models using only BF16, FP8, and FP4.

problem: Multimodal deception in vision-language models remains unexplored, and text-centric monitoring approaches fail to detect deceptive visual reasoning.
approach: Introduces MM-DeceptionBench for evaluating deception across six categories and proposes debate with images—a multi-agent framework enforcing visual grounding through adversarial debate.
contribution: Achieves up to 1.5× improvement in Cohen's kappa and 1.25× in accuracy over MLLM-as-a-judge baselines.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting from sparse views produces artifacts due to insufficient information in under-constrained regions, and generative priors fail to maintain consistency with observations.
approach: GSFixer uses a reference-guided video diffusion model with semantic and geometric features from foundation models, plus reference-guided trajectory sampling for angular coverage.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in 3DGS artifact restoration and sparse-view reconstruction.

problem: Existing safety attribution methods for LLMs struggle with generalization and reliability due to heuristic, domain-specific metrics and search algorithms.
approach: SafeSeek uses differentiable binary masks to extract multi-granular safety circuits via gradient descent, integrating Safety Circuit Tuning for efficient fine-tuning.
contribution: Identifies backdoor circuits (0.42% sparsity) that reduce attack success rate from 100% to 0.4%, and alignment circuits whose removal increases ASR from 0.8% to 96.9%.

problem: Optimizing classification under group fairness sufficiency constraints while maintaining Bayes-optimality requires handling trade-offs between different fairness criteria.
approach: Derives exact solution for optimal binary classification under sufficiency using finite group-calibrated scores, providing geometric characterization of feasible PPV and FOR pairs.
contribution: Simple post-processing algorithm attains optimal classifier and identifies when minimizing separation deviation subject to sufficiency is achievable.

problem: Understanding how network motifs shape collective neural dynamics in artificial neural networks remains unclear despite their importance in biological inspiration.
approach: Analyzes meta-connectivity structure using 13 network motifs as functional building blocks, classifying them into hierarchical dynamical regimes and showing motif distributions shape collective dynamics.
contribution: Provides theoretical framework showing how motifs selectively enhance network robustness or flexibility through underlying dynamics.

problem: Offline policy improvement faces conflict between maximizing value and fitting the data distribution, with gradient-based approaches exhibiting fitting-optimization conflicts.
approach: SPAR reframes improvement as local residual rectification anchored to frozen behavior cloning policy, using Latent Self-Imitation with weighted regression to eliminate manifold-normal drift.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art D4RL performance by extracting significant gains from suboptimal baselines.

problem: Reward models for computer-using agents lack systematic evaluation frameworks, with existing approaches unclear on effectiveness for step-level and trajectory-level assessment.
approach: CUARewardBench provides first comprehensive benchmark for outcome and process reward models on CUA tasks, with trajectories from 10 software categories, expert annotation, and UPE ensemble method.
contribution: Reveals critical limitations in current CUA reward models and shows general VLMs outperform specialized CUA models.

problem: Existing methods for structured diagram generation rely on pixel-based synthesis which is inherently limited in editability and fidelity for professional workflows.
approach: Proposes Diagram-as-Code paradigm using mxGraph XML for precise generation and editing, with VCG-Bench dataset of 1,449 diagrams and multi-dimensional evaluation metrics.
contribution: Reveals challenges faced by current VLMs in structured fidelity and instruction compliance through systematic evaluation.

problem: General-purpose deep learning frameworks suffer from mismatch between dense parallel optimization and irregular tree-structured complexity of biophysical neural network simulation.
approach: HelioX adopts GPU-to-Biophysics paradigm with custom-fused CUDA kernels for Dendritic Hierarchical Scheduling and gradient propagation, enabling efficient multi-stream concurrency.
contribution: Outperforms NEURON by orders of magnitude and enables training of whole-brain-scale biophysical circuits on single consumer GPU.

problem: Individual LLM reasoning approaches suffer from complementary errors—one model succeeds where another fails on the same problem—without mechanism to leverage peer success.
approach: CoRe training converts peer success into learning signal via cross-teaching protocol: cold independent sampling followed by contexted rescue round with peer hints, optimized via combined reward.
contribution: Two small models (3B+4B) reach 99.54% oracle Team Pass@2 on GSM8K with only 1,000 examples, substantially outperforming single-model training.

problem: Forgery detection becomes obsolete as generative AI achieves hyper-realism, and resource-intensive fine-tuning approaches fail to leverage inherent forgery sensitivity in pre-trained models.
approach: DNA framework uses coarse-to-fine excavation to identify forgery-discriminative units (FDUs) within pre-trained models via feature decoupling and attention analysis, without retraining.
contribution: Achieves superior detection even under few-shot conditions with remarkable robustness across architectures and unseen generative models.

problem: Existing safety evaluations for autonomous agents trade off between costly manual benchmarks and scalable but hallucination-prone LLM-based simulators.
approach: AutoControl Arena uses logic-narrative decoupling: deterministic state in executable code while delegating generative dynamics to LLMs, instantiated through three-agent framework.
contribution: Achieves 98% end-to-end success with 60% human preference over simulators; reveals alignment illusions and divergent misalignment patterns across 9 frontier models.

problem: Audio-Visual Segmentation models rely on dense cross-modal attention with quadratic computational cost, limiting deployment on resource-constrained devices.
approach: LightAVSeg replaces attention with decoupled design for semantic filtering and spatial grounding with linear cost, plus auxiliary alignment loss.
contribution: With 20.5M parameters (~1/7 of AVSegFormer), reaches 50.4 mIoU on MS3 benchmark and enables efficient mobile processor inference.

problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts architectures for multimodal learning lack proper handling of missing modalities, leading to performance degradation and poor generalization.
approach: ConfSMoE introduces two-stage imputation module and novel expert gating by detaching softmax routing score to task confidence score, relieving expert collapse without load-balance loss.
contribution: Shows expert collapse aligns across Gaussian and Laplacian gates; comprehensive evaluation demonstrates improved resistance to missing modality.
